r4FindingResolution.reason: QD-28 replaces the impossible notification interval with exact integer equality of the same /proc field-22 key, requires equal time namespaces and a usable unique match, retains unmatched host values, and marks unresolved joins incomplete. The start-before-notification case is explicitly included. This fixes the host join; the separate terminal-counter attribution rule has a new error.

requiredFindings.title: One fork inside the window does not exclude a predecessor's terminal counter
requiredFindings.relation: New error in the replacement for fork-timestamp attribution
requiredFindings.problem: The replacement rule counts new-group forks only between sentinels and attributes records for a unique TGID without ordering. A predecessor born before the window can terminate during it, then the same TGID can be reused for a subtree process. Only the latter's birth is counted, although both generations can produce records. Terminal selection still uses ac_tgid and AGROUP, not the QD-28 start key.
counterexample: Outside process A with TGID p is alive before the pre-launch sentinels. It exits during the run and emits a low taskstats terminal counter.
A becomes reapable and its TGID is released. A's connector exit can be delayed after the reaping notification; A's taskstats record is still pending in the independent userspace receive path.
Subtree B is created with TGID p. It is the only new-group fork(p) inside the window, so the declared uniqueness check passes.
A's taskstats record is consumed after B's fork and accepted as B's ac_tgid=p/AGROUP terminal record under the no-order attribution rule.

B's real taskstats report is omitted because prepare_reply allocation fails. The kernel can return before emitting a packet or allocating a sequence number, so no receive ENOBUFS or connector sequence gap is required.

B's connector exit and every post-run sentinel arrive. A's connector exit can arrive later than those fences; B's required exit is already present. There is one accepted terminal record and no duplicate.
B has no host entry, explicitly allowed by line 794. Therefore the exact host-start join cannot detect that B's missing own counter was replaced by A's counter.
requiredFindings.impact: All stated per-run predicates can be satisfied with the wrong, lower own-counter value. If the brief B peak also falls between concurrent samples, RSS can be understated and an incomplete run can be reported complete and potentially within budget.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Require a positive way to exclude predecessor records and bind each accepted terminal counter to the lifetime opened for the subtree. One in-window birth alone is insufficient. Define how pre-window occupants and delayed outside/pre-opening terminal/exit traffic are retained and reconciled through completion, or use another generation-safe counter identity. Any attribution that cannot be proven must remain incomplete. Add a design/calibration case for a pre-window outside predecessor, in-window TGID reuse, delayed predecessor delivery and a missing successor taskstats report.

sources.evidence: prepare_reply can fail allocation before taskstats sequence allocation (70-74); taskstats_exit returns on that failure without a report (592-594). AGROUP is applied to the per-task record at 600-602.
taskstats_exit occurs at 888 before exit_notify at 923 and proc_exit_connector at 924, permitting the predecessor notification/counter delivery order described.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Make the PID namespace and proc-view requirement explicit
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The same-pair interface requirement should explicitly require compatible initial-namespace TGIDs and the corresponding /proc view, as well as equal time namespaces. Taskstats/connector report initial-namespace IDs; a host-side namespace-relative TGID is not interchangeable. The existing requirement that the host supply the same pair can already impose this, so it is an interface clarification under OI-11 rather than an additional required finding.

withdrawalAssessment.rejectingObservedReuse: Sound and conservative: multiple observed births for a subtree TGID force incomplete.
withdrawalAssessment.claimedUniqueGeneration: Not established by one birth within the sentinel window; C2-Q0-R5-01 covers the boundary predecessor case.
withdrawalAssessment.exactHostBridge: Sound for usable equal keys in the required common namespace/proc representation, with unresolved joins retained and incomplete.

referenceCaseInspection.method: Static inspection only; no reference implementation or validator run.
referenceCaseInspection.hostJoinCases: The stated equality, failed/inconsistent read, key mismatch, observed double birth and time-namespace cases agree with QD-28. They do not cover predecessor generations born before the window.
referenceCaseInspection.quantityMapping: host-join-unresolved is admitted by ENV runReason and carried by slotReasons. QD-27 removes ownHighWaterSumBytes and peakRssBytes, retains elapsed/concurrent samples and eligible median, and keeps the batch incomplete/non-Q6.

scopeAssessment.description: All changes map to revision metadata/table, exact start-key acquisition/host join, replacement TGID uniqueness attribution, calibration/reference cases, the new QD-27 reason and QD-28 index. The schema changes only its revision/validator description and adds host-join-unresolved to runReason. The new required finding is within the declared replacement attribution rule.

verification.method: Read-only comparison of r5 with retained r4 subjects/review and static checks against primary Linux v6.18 source.
